Bulk transfers maintain good throughput while interactive requests become slow on the same link. You are examining the behavior of queues under sustained demand.

Which TWO statements correctly describe queueing and the relevant operational constraints? Select exactly two answers.
options: More buffering can trade packet loss for queueing delay
Increasing every buffer always lowers latency
Queue depth has no relationship to request delay
Packets wait longer before transmission under sustained congestion

questions.objective: Explain queueing and apply it to an operational decision.
questions.takeaway: More buffering can trade packet loss for queueing delay.
questions.explanation: Packets wait longer before transmission under sustained congestion. More buffering can trade packet loss for queueing delay. In the operational case, the appropriate response is: measure queueing delay and evaluate traffic management. As utilization approaches capacity, waiting time can grow sharply. Larger queues delay rejection but do not add service capacity. Bound queues, measure wait time and apply backpressure or shedding when deadlines can no longer be met.
